blocks.md: Store immutable blobs as independently readable blocks. Each block is framed, optionally compressed, and checksummed so a small random read never requires decoding an unrelated blob.

blocks.label: FIG 1
blocks.caption: Compression and integrity are block-local. That locality is what makes exact random reads cheap and bounded.

blocks.title: Validate before allocating
blocks.md: Lengths come from stored bytes that may be corrupt. Reject impossible raw or encoded lengths before allocating or decompressing; otherwise a tiny corrupt header can become a memory bomb.

blocks.label: What you implement
blocks.code: func OpenStore(dir string, device contract.Device, memoryLimit uint64) (contract.Store, error)

blocks.explain: The request overlaps only the second block. Find that block through the index, verify and decode it, then copy the requested slice. Do not read the first block.

items: A blob key is the pair `(id, version)`; duplicates return `contract.ErrDuplicate`.
Store compressed bytes only when they are strictly smaller than raw bytes.
Verify frame lengths and CRC-32 before returning data.
`Close` is terminal and idempotent; the easy tier's `Compact` is a no-op.

items.title: Design the frame
items.md: Keep enough metadata to locate, bound, decode, and verify one block.

items.title: Index physical ranges
items.md: Map each blob version and logical block number to its device offset and encoded length.

items.title: Read only overlap
items.md: Translate the requested logical range into the minimum set of blocks before touching the device.

blocks.title: The trade-off
blocks.md: Smaller blocks improve random-read locality but add more headers and index entries. Larger blocks reduce metadata while making each small read decode more data.
